identity.name: compute_parcel_cost_estimates
identity.description: Single-phase ENRICHER: streams every residential parcel (zoning_class LIKE 'R%') through the pure pricing engine (scripts/lib/parcel-cost.js) and writes a 13-line renovation-cost menu (JSONB) + 12 headline cost scalars + 3 FSI scalars, one JS-streamed cursor-batched post_commit phase, each batch flushed through its own short transaction. PURE PARCEL MODEL — external industry cost only (archetype_cost_rates); no permit data, no declared cost, no Liar's Gate (Spec 88 §1). CPCE-A1 RULED (Spec 124 R-AR.1): the Phase-B-B3 run-ledger gate is RETIRED as a mechanism — this ENRICHER's runner shape has no gated-skip branch and this step has no lineage-stamp column to hold a Layer-2 predicate; every invocation streams the whole declared population and the 16-column IS DISTINCT FROM write guard keeps a steady-state re-run's write count near zero.

why_lock.text: Spec 47 §A.5 — lock 88 (the owning spec number) is taken by classify-permits.js (predates the spec-number convention); 117 is the assigned free-ID from the post-Wave-7 range, ported verbatim from the pre-conversion `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 117` and agreeing with pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts:143. O1 CORRECTION (2026-09-21): this sentence previously (falsely) claimed the audit_table `phase` key still carries the spec number (88) — it does not; see `sharing.varies_by_chain.phase.sources` and the deviations[] entry below for the actual (fleet-standard) value.

guard_columns_why.text: The verbatim 16-column guard, legacy `distinctGuard = ['parcel_cost_menu', ...ALL_SCALAR_COLS]`. All 16 are in the guard — the mechanism that makes a re-run against unchanged inputs write ~0 rows instead of re-pricing 437,279 parcels every invocation (measured live: 77/190 of 437,281 candidates on the two July ledger rows).

why.text: CPCE-A1 RULED (operator, 2026-09-21, Spec 124 R-AR.1) — knowingly-retired. `runEnrichPhase` has no `ledgerGatedSkip` call (measured: only `runCascadePhase`/`runMaterializePhase` call it) and this step has no lineage-stamp column to hold a Layer-2 predicate — the 2.2 (enrich_heritage) remedy is structurally unavailable here. Every scheduled run now streams the whole declared population; the 16-column IS DISTINCT FROM guard keeps the write cost low in steady state. F9's version-signal stamps SURVIVE as emits[]-only observability. The cloud no-op cost of this retirement is UNMEASURED and is a declared, carried risk (limitations[]), resolved at the end-of-batch cloud proof.

deviations.from: the legacy's D#3 atomic co-read of the escalation-index VALUE and its version stamp, both from ONE query, inside the lock

why.text: FOLD-V9(2) (binding amendment) — the priced VALUE is now `ctx.config.cost_escalation_index` (declared, LM-D15-validated, hoisted above the lock, per Spec 122 §1.2a P4 — a defaulted/ad hoc re-read would make test 5's literal scan and the engine signature contradict each other). `readCostContract`'s own re-read of the same logic_variables row is retained ONLY for the `index_updated_at` version stamp (emits[]). Because `runEnrichPhase` itself executes inside `pipeline.withAdvisoryLock`, the contract_read hook still runs under the same lock the legacy's D#3 read did — the torn-read window this fence existed to close is not re-opened for the CONCURRENT-EDIT case; the one narrowed difference is that the priced value comes from the step-wide hoisted config rather than a second identical read.

PARCEL_COST_LINES (13 lines) and PERMITTED_VALUES are policy tables in source, not admin-visible (CPCE-A3 RULED). archetype_cost_rates (12 rows × 3 pricing fields) is the largest tunable surface this step consumes and is a DB table read via inputs.reads.tables, NOT counted toward the 'all variables externalized' claim (CPCE-A4 RULED) — it is ported byte-for-byte. An admin editor for both is a separate filed WF.

realized_fsi_p90 is declared both a read and a write; every value written is NULL (a P1 sentinel — P2's family-aware norm read populates it). CPCE-A9(ii) — declared here, not dropped from the write set (dropping it would change the 16-column guard).

Two non-step analysis consumers of the ENGINE (not the columns) require the config argument as a REQUIRED positional now: scripts/analysis/wf3-cost-coherence-sanity.js and scripts/analysis/wf3-sample-full-dump.js — updated in this commit to read-live-else-seed-default the 6 engine tunables (FOLD-I5/V8).

recovery.reset: No TRUNCATE/rebuild mechanism and none is needed — a plain re-run re-streams the whole R% population (staleness.scope 'all') and the 16-column IS DISTINCT FROM guard makes an unnecessary re-write cheap.

interrupted_why.text: Unlike a shared-txn ENRICHER, this step has NO shared transaction (`execution.txn_scope:"none"`) — each ctx.flushBatch call is its OWN short transaction, so a run killed mid-stream leaves already-flushed batches COMMITTED (execution.partial_fill:"staged"). 'none' is the honest recovery value (no special action needed), NOT `force_full_on_next_run`: staleness.scope is unconditionally 'all' already, so the very next run re-streams and re-prices every row regardless of whether the prior run was interrupted, converging without any special-cased recovery branch. Proven by the new compute-parcel-cost-kill-mid-run.db.test.ts (pg_cancel_backend, not a process kill).

before_image_why.text: recovery.before_image applies to a retraction (outputs.writes[].retract != 'none'); this step's sole write target declares retract:'none' — it only ever stamps a value, never clears one to NULL as a distinct operation.

why.text: A4 ruling — declares the scanned residential population (NOT 13× the per-line counts, §2.11 counter scoping). matched.compute.<name> resolves while a bare compute.* resolves NULL for every ENRICHER.

CPCE-D5 CLOSED (cutover ③, 2026-09-21) — was the literal string "null", which COUNTER-ROOT (#26; only scans converted[] descriptors, so this was invisible before cutover) rejects as an unresolvable root for shape "enrich". Corrected to the fleet-standard form every sibling ENRICHER uses (enrich_heritage, enrich_ravines, geocode_permits, enrich_parcels — all `matched.compute.records_new_aggregate`): this step INSERTs nothing — the sole write target is an UPDATE, and class N's own executor structurally refuses any statement text containing INSERT INTO or ON CONFLICT (JOIN_UPDATE_FORBIDDEN_RE, scripts/lib/step/write.js) — `records_new_aggregate: 0` is a declared finite literal, already returned by computePostPhase's `compute:` block, because an omitted/null source resolves as "not counted" rather than the true zero it is (Spec 48 §3.6).

COUNTER-ROOT (FOLD-I8, restated): `ctx.flushBatch` is a bare BEGIN/query/COMMIT wrapper — it is NEVER seam-owned (only `ctx.retract`/`ctx.joinUpdate` populate `seamOwned`). So `index.js`'s `!seamOwned` branch always applies for this target, and `written.e1.updated` is filled from the pass's own returned `{updated, scanned}` (§5 test 6, both directions).
